name: Indian Forest Service Officer
title: Indian Forest Service (IFoS)
intro: From Class 12 Science to an IFoS officer: an eligible science, agriculture, forestry or engineering degree, the Civil Services Prelims as the screening test, the IFoS Mains and interview, then training and state cadre postings.

phases.title: Class 12 Science
phases.summary: PCM or PCB leads to the eligible degrees.
points: Science at Class 12 leads to the eligible degrees (science subjects, agriculture, forestry, veterinary or engineering).
Commerce and Arts do not lead to the listed degrees.
Physical fitness matters later — there is a walking test.

phases.title: An eligible bachelor's degree
phases.summary: A listed science subject, or agriculture, forestry or engineering.
points: A bachelor's with at least one of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Science, Botany, Chemistry, Geology, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics or Zoology.
Or a bachelor's in Agriculture, Forestry or Engineering.
Age limits, attempts and relaxations are in the UPSC notice.

phases.title: Civil Services Prelims (screening)
phases.summary: Apply for IFoS in the same application; prelims screens candidates.
points: IFoS uses the Civil Services Preliminary Examination as its screening test.
You apply for IFoS in the same application as the Civil Services exam.
The Mains and interview for IFoS are separate from the CSE ones.

phases.title: IFoS Mains and interview
phases.summary: General English, General Knowledge and two optional subjects, then a personality test.
points: IFoS Mains: written papers including General English, General Knowledge and two optional subjects.
Those who qualify face a personality test by UPSC.
Medical and physical standards apply, including the walking test UPSC specifies.

phases.title: Training, posting and growth
phases.summary: Training, then state cadre postings in the forest department.
points: Entry: Group A central services start at Level 10 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (₹56,100 entry basic), plus DA, HRA and other allowances.
Growth path: Assistant Conservator (training) → DCF → Conservator → CCF → PCCF, who heads a state forest department.
State forest services (ACF, Range Forest Officer) are recruited separately by state PSCs.
